title: Tracing and Attribution: Blockchain Analytics in Practice
summary: How investigators and service providers trace funds across public ledgers, cluster and attribute addresses, and how far analytics outputs can be relied on as intelligence or evidence.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How investigators and service providers trace funds across public ledgers, cluster and attribute addresses, and how far analytics outputs can be relied on as intelligence or evidence.
Learning Objectives: Explain the main tracing techniques and clustering heuristics
Interpret risk scores, exposure reports and attribution data critically
Assess the evidential value and limits of analytics outputs
Syllabus: Traceability on public ledgers: following inputs and outputs
Clustering, attribution and labelling of services and illicit actors
Risk scoring, false positives and gaps in coverage
From analytics to evidence: documentation, reproducibility and expert testimony
Intended Audience: AML/CFT supervisors and inspectors responsible for crypto-asset service providers
FIU analysts handling crypto-related suspicious transaction reports and intelligence
Law-enforcement and financial crime investigators working on cases involving crypto-assets
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT supervision, financial intelligence or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
